script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for QQQ. Tuesday — here is your QQQ recap. The portfolio closed three point one eight percent up on the session.

Semiconductor stocks lit up Tuesday. Intel and Sandisk each surged ten point eight four percent, Micron jumped seven point six two, and Advanced Micro Devices gained seven percent. The chip complex dominated this session from open to close.

The broad market staged a convincing rally on Tuesday, driven by a combination of stronger-than-expected corporate earnings and easing geopolitical tension after reported progress in United States-Iran negotiations sent oil prices sharply lower. The Nasdaq led major indices higher, reflecting renewed appetite for growth and technology names across the board.

Bank of America reiterated its buy rating on Micron and maintained a price target of one thousand five hundred fifty dollars, calling Tuesday's earlier pullback a buying opportunity. The bank's thesis centers on end-demand from cloud and artificial intelligence infrastructure, which it describes as solidly on track. Micron closed up seven point six two percent on the session, making it the second-strongest performer among primary holdings. When a tier-one bank publicly reiterates a four-digit price target against a backdrop of sector-wide strength in memory and storage, the message to the market is clear: the AI infrastructure buildout is generating real, durable demand for memory, and Micron sits directly in that current.

Now to the full rundown, starting with the largest positions.

Nvidia gained two point five six percent on Tuesday. The session's broad rally, which theetfbully.com attributed to strong earnings across the market and falling oil prices tied to geopolitical progress, provided tailwind for the entire semiconductor space. Watch Nvidia heading into any further earnings catalysts from AI infrastructure customers later this week.

Apple gained one point nine six percent on the session. The headline story here is India — annual sales reportedly crossed ten billion dollars for the first time, per Yahoo Finance, as both retail expansion and domestic manufacturing continue to scale. That is a meaningful geographic diversification story. The ongoing OpenAI trade secret litigation, where OpenAI released internal Apple employee communications to contest the suit, bears watching but carries no immediate financial read-through.

Alphabet gained one point one one percent on Tuesday. An analysis from Yahoo Finance argues the stock could be fourteen percent undervalued despite fresh legal scrutiny — Teads Holding has filed suit in New York accusing Google of exclusionary advertising technology practices. The seven-day return cited in that piece is eleven point nine three percent following recent earnings. The antitrust overhang is real, but the valuation gap thesis is gaining traction among analysts.

Micron jumped seven point six two percent, as covered in the top story. Bank of America's reaffirmed buy thesis and the broad memory sector strength drove the move. Watch for any forward guidance commentary from storage-adjacent names this week.

Microsoft gained one point zero six percent on the session. No specific company news drove the move — this was a broad technology tape lift. Microsoft remains the portfolio's fifth-largest position and continues to trade in lockstep with enterprise cloud sentiment.

Amazon was down two point three two percent on Tuesday, making it the lone notable decliner among primary holdings. No company-specific catalyst was identified for the move. Consumer discretionary softness may have weighed, or profit-taking after recent strength. The divergence from the broader tape warrants monitoring.

Advanced Micro Devices surged seven point zero zero percent on Tuesday. The move aligns with the broader semiconductor rally that lifted Intel, Micron, and storage names simultaneously. No single company-specific catalyst was identified, but the artificial intelligence accelerator narrative continues to support the stock.

Tesla gained one point six four percent on the session. No specific news was attributed to the move. The stock tracked the broader market higher, consistent with a risk-on session. Upcoming production and delivery data remain the next material catalysts for this position.

Intel surged ten point eight four percent on Tuesday — the strongest single-day move among all primary holdings. Turning briefly to Sandisk, also up ten point eight four percent in the secondary holdings, the synchrony of those two moves alongside Lam Research's seven point eight five percent gain and Applied Materials' five point four eight percent advance suggests a coordinated rotation into semiconductor capital equipment and legacy chip names. Intel's move is the more consequential for this portfolio given its primary position weight.

Three items to track in the next forty-eight hours. First, Parker-Hannifin reports fourth-quarter earnings on August sixth — its shares are up more than thirty-seven percent year to date, and industrial earnings have been a key broad market driver Tuesday. Second, any further development in United States-Iran diplomatic talks could move oil materially, with knock-on effects for the growth and technology trade. Third, watch for additional analyst commentary on Alphabet's ad technology litigation, as the fourteen percent undervaluation thesis will attract scrutiny and response from the sell side.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for QQQ. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. The semiconductor complex is running hot — whether that momentum carries or consolidates into Wednesday will be the defining question for this portfolio.
